properties.name: Maharbiz Lab — Neural Dust
properties.description:
**Michel Maharbiz** — University of California, Berkeley, Berkeley, CA (US)

Co-inventor (with Jose Carmena, Elad Alon, Jan Rabaey) of 'neural dust' -- an ultrasonic power and communication platform for vanishingly small, batteryless, tetherless implants that record and transmit neural activity. Group works broadly on extreme miniaturization of synthetic interfaces to cells and organisms; also known for the earlier radio-controlled cyborg beetle work.

[[https://people.eecs.berkeley.edu/~maharbiz/index.html|Group website]]

Category: Neuroscience Lab · Smallest demonstrated: unknown

properties.name: iota Biosciences
properties.description:
**iota Biosciences** — iota Biosciences, Inc., Alameda, CA (US)

Commercializing neural dust: millimeter-sized bioelectronic implants wirelessly powered and read out via ultrasound, able to record and stimulate nerve activity and communicate with other devices via ultrasound backscatter. Founded 2017 by Jose Carmena and Michel Maharbiz out of their UC Berkeley research; acquired by Astellas Pharma in 2020. As of 2024, has an FDA investigational device exemption for an early feasibility study in underactive bladder treatment.

[[https://iota.bio/|Group website]]

Category: Neuroscience Lab · Smallest demonstrated: unknown

properties.name: Robinson Lab — Nano-neurotechnology
properties.description:
**Jacob T. Robinson** — Rice University, Houston, TX (US)

Uses semiconductor nanofabrication and genetic engineering to build electronic, photonic, and magnetic interfaces to the brain. Co-authored a magnetoelectric backscatter communication system for bioelectronic implants achieving <0.3 pJ/bit and <1e-6 bit error rate at 55 mm range with 10 mm misalignment tolerance, demonstrated transmitting cardiac signals from a beating heart in a porcine model. PI Jacob T. Robinson is also co-founder/CEO of Motif Neurotech (brain-computer interface for mental health disorders).

[[https://www.robinsonlab.com/|Group website]]

Category: Neuroscience Lab · Smallest demonstrated: unknown

properties.name: Synchron
properties.description:
**Synchron** — Synchron, Brooklyn, NY (US)

Developing the Stentrode, an implantable brain-computer interface delivered endovascularly (through blood vessels, no open-brain surgery) to a vein next to the motor cortex, connected to a subcutaneous antenna that transmits neural data out of the body wirelessly. Implanted in six US patients as of the referenced study; targeting a 2026 pivotal trial toward the first FDA-approved BCI. Backed by Bezos and Gates, among others.

[[https://synchron.com/|Group website]]

Category: Neuroscience Lab · Smallest demonstrated: unknown
